_note: Carlos Aster, your advisor: the voice of the interface. Each line has an id; a recording saved as godot/assets/voice/carlos/<id>.ogg (or .wav) plays with it. 'tutorial' lines play in order on the first month; the rest are picked at random without repeating until a situation's lines run out. He spins, but never lies about a number: the numbers are always shown next to him.

tutorial.text: Boss! Welcome to headquarters. It's not much yet: a desk, a map, a kettle. But it's yours, and I've got a feeling about you.
The board on the left is what needs you right now. The map shows who leads where. Everything else is in the files along the top.
The whole country argues about something every month. Open Debates, pick a side, and say it your way. People remember how you said it.
You get three moves a month. Speak, start your own argument, open an office somewhere, dig into the competition. No wrong answers, boss. Well. Mostly.
When you're ready, press play and the weeks roll on. I'll be right here. I'm always right here.

month_start.text: New month, boss. Three fresh moves. The country's waiting.
A new month! I've cleared your diary. Well, I've cleared it of things I didn't think you'd enjoy.
Morning, boss. Coffee's on the desk, the debates are on the board.
Another month. You know, I keep a list of everything you get right. I need a bigger notebook.
Three moves this month. Make them count. Not that you'd do anything else.
Fresh month, fresh headlines. Somebody out there is saying something you could answer.

poll_up.text: Up! Up, boss! I told the office you'd do this. I told them in writing.
The poll's up. The pollsters are finally catching up with what I already knew.
That's the trend, boss. That's the beginning of something.
Another rise. At this rate I'll have to learn how to address a minister.
Look at that line go. It's your instincts, boss. You can't teach that.

poll_down.text: A small dip. Pollsters. They phone people during dinner and expect honesty.
It's down a little, but the people who matter haven't moved. I checked. Well, I'm fairly sure.
Polls go up, polls go down. Your vision stays the same. That's what they'll remember.
Margins of error, boss. Margins of error everywhere you look.
A dip before the jump. Every great comeback starts with one.

poll_flat.text: Steady. Solid. A foundation, boss. You can build a palace on a foundation.
Holding firm while everyone else wobbles. That's leadership.
No change this month. The calm before something, I'd say.

annual_poll.text: The big December poll is in, region by region. I've read it twice. I liked it more the second time.
The annual numbers, boss. A year of your work, all on one sheet of paper.

budget.text: Budget time! The fun part. Where shall we put the money, boss?
The quarterly ledger. I've sharpened your pencils.
Money in, money out. You always know where it does the most good.
A few donors have been in touch. Generous people. Very generous. I'm sure it's because they believe in you.

event.text: Something's happened, boss. Every channel wants your reaction.
Big news. The country's turning to you for an answer.
The phones are ringing. They want you, boss. Specifically you.
A story's breaking. Whatever you say, say it like you mean it.

viral.text: It's everywhere! My cousin sent it to me. My cousin doesn't even like politics!
That clip is on every phone in Cranebo. They're making songs out of it, boss.
Did you see that? Of course you did. You were there. You were magnificent.
That's the one they'll play at your retirement party. Decades from now, obviously.

gaffe.text: I think you made a great point, boss.
Bold. Very bold. The country isn't ready for that kind of honesty yet. They will be.
The commentators didn't get it. Commentators never get it.
Let's call that a conversation starter.

speak.text: Lovely. I'd have said it the same way. Well, not as well.
That one's going on the wall.
They'll be quoting that in the cafés tonight.

raise_caught.text: It caught! Everyone's arguing about it now. And who started it? You did.
That's agenda-setting, boss. Textbook. They'll write textbooks.
The whole country took the bait. I mean, took up the issue.

raise_fizzled.text: Ahead of its time, boss. Ideas like that need a few months to ripen.
The papers buried it. Their loss. Literally, their readers' loss.
Not everyone's ready to hear the truth on a Tuesday.

major_debate.text: This one's big, boss. The whole country's arguing. Whatever you say gets quoted.
Everyone's talking about it. If you're going to say something, now's the time. If you're not, that's a statement too.

community.text: A new office! I've ordered a sign. A big one.
Volunteers, a noticeboard and a kettle. That's how empires start, boss.
The locals love it. Well, the ones who came. They brought cake.

steer.text: A new direction. Visionary. Some of our people will grumble, but they always come round. Mostly.
Changing course takes courage. Lucky we have plenty.

figure_quit.text: Between us, boss, they were holding you back.
One door closes. Frankly, it was a draughty door.
They'll regret it. People always do, once you've won.

dirty_money.text: Generous people, those donors. And so discreet.
Money's money, boss. It doesn't come with opinions. Usually.

debate_night.text: Tonight's the big debate. Lights, cameras, and you. They don't stand a chance.
The final debate, boss. Just be yourself. Your self is very electable.

election_near.text: Three months to the election. I've stopped sleeping. You should keep sleeping; one of us needs to look fresh.
The home stretch, boss. Every move counts double now. Well, it feels that way.

won.text: We did it! You did it! I always said so. I have it in writing!
The largest party in the Assembly. I'd like to say I'm surprised, boss, but I'm not.

lost.text: The country wasn't ready for you, boss. Not yet.
A moral victory. The best kind. The other kind is overrated.

tip.text: Tip, boss: a story already in the headlines is far easier to turn into a national argument.
Speak for the sides that are yours. Heat on someone else's issue warms someone else's voters.
Offices take a while to pay off, but they never stop working. Like me.
Provocative lines catch fire. Sometimes the fire is on us. Mostly it's on them.
Say the same kind of thing often enough and people start to recognise your voice. That's charisma, boss.
If an argument is helping the competition, change the subject. Nobody notices. Nobody important.
Staying out of a fight is allowed. Nobody can quote what you didn't say.
Business money is easy money. Just don't let anyone see the receipt.
The Country file lists every problem we could talk about. Problems are opportunities, boss.
Your causes are your brand. Two is the limit; pick the ones with the most angry voters.
